nodes.label: Skin Cancer RAG-Enhanced Chatbot Design Spec
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Adds a RAG layer plus a Flask-to-FastAPI refactor because the original chatbot hit the OpenAI API with no domain grounding, which is a hallucination risk in healthcare.
nodes.norm_label: skin cancer rag-enhanced chatbot design spec

nodes.label: Three-Layer Mandatory Medical Disclaimer
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 (system prompt) is vulnerable to prompt injection, so layer 2 (deterministic post-generation regex force-append) is added as the bypass-proof guarantee, and layer 3 (persistent UI footer) is independent of the LLM entirely. Defense in depth because a missing disclaimer is a compliance failure, not a UX bug.

nodes.label: Evidence Filter (Cosine Similarity Threshold)
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Retrieve top-10 then drop chunks below a conservative 0.7 cosine threshold, overshooting before filtering. Motivated directly by the 'Rethinking RAG for Medicine' finding that raw RAG can degrade medical answer quality — a conservative gate is preferred to more context.

nodes.label: LCEL RAG Chain (retriever | prompt | llm)
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: LCEL rather than LangGraph in v1 for simplicity; the agentic grader loop is deferred to Phase 4 as an explicit YAGNI cut with a clear evolution path. Chain is stateless with injected dependencies and no globals so it can be unit-tested without a server.

nodes.label: Single Multilingual Prompt Template
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: One template serves both ID and EN because modern LLMs are sufficiently multilingual; maintaining two near-identical templates costs maintenance without quality benefit. Only the disclaimer needs hardcoded per-language versions.

nodes.label: LLMProvider Protocol + Factory
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Protocol plus env-var factory so swapping OpenAI for Ollama/vLLM is a config change, never a caller change; success metric is that the swap is verified by integration test with only an env var edit.

nodes.label: VectorStoreProvider Protocol + Factory
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: ChromaDB chosen as default because it is local, free, and privacy-friendly for healthcare data; Pinecone stubbed behind the same Protocol as a future swap path rather than deployed.

nodes.label: Semantic Chunking Ingestion Pipeline
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Percentile-breakpoint semantic chunking at 500-800 tokens with 100-token overlap, embedded in batches of 100 and upserted with SHA256 hash-based chunk IDs so re-running ingestion is idempotent.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Knowledge Base (Guidelines + PubMed)
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 is patient-education guidelines (AAD, MedlinePlus, DermNet NZ) for trust and plain language; Tier 2 is curated PubMed abstracts for deeper questions. Unified single index rather than two indexes, deferring intent routing to a later phase. Licensing drove selection: AAD/MedlinePlus free for education, DermNet CC BY-NC-ND acceptable for academic use.

nodes.label: Pre-LLM Dangerous Query Classifier
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Four categories (safe_medical, safe_general, unsafe_dosage, off_topic); keyword/regex heuristics handle obvious cases cheaply and a gpt-4o-mini zero-shot prompt is reserved for ambiguous ones to keep per-call cost near $0.0001.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Defense
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: System-prompt rule 7 plus input pattern flagging plus 'output is always text, never executable'. Explicitly acknowledged as insufficient alone — the deterministic disclaimer force-append is the actual bypass-proof control.

nodes.label: SHA256 Query Hashing for Logs
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Raw query text is never persisted; only a SHA256 hash plus non-identifying counters go to logs/rag_usage.log. Success criterion is 'zero raw PII in logs', verified by grepping log files.

nodes.label: Inline [n] Citation Markers
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Markers are inline in the streamed text, but the full source list can only be rendered after the stream completes since only then is it known which numbers the answer actually used. Practice borrowed from MMed-RAG and MedRGB.

nodes.label: Bounded 6-Turn Session Memory
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Last 6 turns (3 exchanges) per session; the detection result is injected once at conversation start rather than repeated every turn to save tokens. Session loss on restart is explicitly accepted as low-impact — start fresh with no error surfaced.

nodes.label: SSE Token Streaming via StreamingResponse
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Native FastAPI support and better perceived latency than waiting for a full response; target is first token under 2s even with p95 total under 8s.

nodes.label: 30-Question Bilingual Eval Gold Set
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: 15 EN + 15 ID questions each annotated with expected source tier and required content. Metrics: recall@5 > 70%, citation accuracy > 90%, disclaimer presence 100%, hallucination < 10%, p95 < 8s, and bilingual parity between the ID and EN subsets.

nodes.label: Framework-Agnostic RAG Module Boundary
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: RAG logic has no FastAPI imports; routes are thin wrappers and schemas are the only framework-specific layer. Buys three things: unit-testing the chain without a server, swapping web frameworks without touching retrieval, and reusing the chain from CLI/notebooks.

nodes.label: Cross-Lingual Embedder (text-embedding-3-small)
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: The KB is English-only but users query in Indonesian, so a cross-lingual embedder is the mitigation for the ID-query/EN-corpus mismatch risk; verification test requires 'kanker kulit' to retrieve 'skin cancer' docs. BGE-m3 is the swap target if moving to a local LLM.

nodes.label: Rethinking RAG for Medicine (2511.06738)
nodes.rationale: Cited as the warning that raw RAG can degrade medical performance; it is the stated motivation for both the evidence filter and the citation discipline.

nodes.label: UI + Folder Restructure Design Spec
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: The v2 RAG backend worked over API only with no UI, and `utils/` was judged too generic a name for business logic. Adds a 3-page UI and renames the package in one pass.

nodes.label: utils/ to services/ Refactor
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Executed with `git mv` to preserve history, pycache removed first so the moves don't fail, ~30 import sites updated, and verified by requiring `grep -r "from utils" .` to return zero and all 64 pre-existing tests to still pass.

nodes.label: Anti-AI-Slop Design Principia
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Explicit ban list — gradient hero, 'AI-powered' copy, 3-column icon grid, generic 'Get Started' CTA, glassmorphism, generic chat bubbles — because each is trendy/characterless and dates fast. Replaced with a flat document-like medical-report aesthetic, definition lists, domain-specific CTAs ('Upload Foto Lesi', 'Klasifikasikan'), and Indonesian healthcare vocabulary (Sp.KK, faktor risiko). Notably, the shipped home.html contradicts several of these.

nodes.label: Clinical Light/Dark Color Palette
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Medical teal + warm neutral + amber + dark slate, no gradients. Dark mode uses slate-900 rather than pure black to keep clinical softness, and teal/amber are brightened in dark to hold WCAG AA contrast.

nodes.label: Tailwind darkMode:'class' Toggle Strategy
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Class toggle on <html> with localStorage persistence, falling back to prefers-color-scheme on first visit only. Tailwind config must be declared before the CDN script loads or darkMode:'class' is ignored.

nodes.label: fetch() + ReadableStream SSE Parsing
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Standard EventSource only supports GET, but /api/chat is a POST carrying session_id/message/detection, so the client must parse the SSE frame format manually off a ReadableStream reader.

nodes.label: Three-Page MVP UI (Home, Upload, Chat)
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Deliberately scoped to three pages: no article pages, no FAQ, no bilingual UI toggle, no browser automation tests. UI chrome is Indonesian-only while chatbot responses stay bilingual.

nodes.label: Tailwind via CDN (No Build Step)
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: No npm and no build step keeps the Python-only toolchain intact; the ~3MB CDN payload is explicitly accepted as fine for a demo/academic deployment. Vanilla JS only — no Alpine.js or HTMX.

nodes.label: Indonesian-Only UI Chrome
nodes.author: Brainstorming session
nodes.rationale: Navbar, buttons, and labels are Bahasa Indonesia only — a bilingual UI toggle is an explicit non-goal — while chatbot responses stay bilingual. Splitting the two lets the interface commit to the Indonesian patient context (Sp.KK, faktor risiko) without duplicating chrome strings.

nodes.label: Empty Knowledge Base Root Cause
nodes.rationale: Chroma held only ~6 chunks from one sample markdown per source and fetch_pubmed.py had never been run. This explained the production symptom where /api/chat returned 200 with num_chunks_retrieved=0 and still produced an ungrounded, uncited answer — a silent failure, not an error.

nodes.label: Incremental Ingest Without --rebuild
nodes.rationale: --rebuild wipes the whole collection; since this task only adds PubMed content, rebuilding is unnecessary churn that risks damaging the already-working aad/dermnet/medlineplus chunks.

nodes.label: RAG_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD Config Discrepancy
nodes.rationale: .env.example suggests 0.7 while config.py defaults to 0.3; at 0.7 retrieval can still return zero results even with data present. Deliberately scoped as report-only — the user decides whether to lower it rather than the agent changing it silently.

nodes.label: SHA256 Idempotent Chunk IDs
nodes.rationale: Chunk IDs are SHA256-derived, so re-running the ingest steps later is safe and cannot duplicate content.

nodes.label: VLM Image Validation + Label-Order Fix Design
nodes.rationale: Two independent defects fixed together purely because they share the image-upload code path (routes/api_routes.py → services/image/).
nodes.norm_label: vlm image validation + label-order fix design

nodes.label: GPT-4o Vision Lesion Validation Gate
nodes.rationale: Without it, faces/objects/scenery get a confident but meaningless skin-cancer label. The legacy Flask app had this gate in utils/validation.py and it was lost in the FastAPI rewrite. Uses AsyncOpenAI natively (no asyncio.to_thread), base64 data URL from in-memory bytes with no temp file, temperature=0 and ~10 max_tokens, and the prompt is ported verbatim from the legacy module.

nodes.label: ValidationUnavailableError (Fail-Closed Signal)
nodes.rationale: Any SDK/network/timeout error or empty API key raises this and maps to 503 with no classification — fail closed. Deliberately asymmetric with the 'uncertain' verdict, which fails OPEN and lets the image through, on the grounds that a parsing hiccup should not reject a real lesion.

nodes.label: SKIN_CANCER_LABELS Order Fix
nodes.rationale: The FastAPI rewrite put Melanoma at index 0, but the trained skinCancer.h5 emits classes in the legacy order, so argmax index 0 (really Karsinoma Sel Basal) was reported as Melanoma; only Nevus at index 3 stayed correct. Preprocessing was explicitly ruled out as the cause — legacy img_to_array and current np.array both feed raw 0-255 RGB at 224x224 with normalization baked into the model — so preprocessing is left unchanged. Fixed in both hardcoding sites (classifier + schemas/detection.py Literal), which an existing test already asserts stay in sync.

nodes.label: Cheap Local Decode Pre-Check
nodes.rationale: Image.open(...).verify() runs before the VLM call so corrupt or non-image bytes are rejected locally with a 400 without spending an OpenAI request. Needed because validation now runs ahead of the classifier, which previously produced that 400.

nodes.label: validation_status Response Field
nodes.rationale: Literal['valid','uncertain'] because only those two verdicts can reach a 200. Exposed specifically so the UI can surface an 'uncertain' advisory rather than presenting a borderline classification as confident.

nodes.label: Bilingual Image Rejection Message
nodes.rationale: Indonesian primary, English secondary, matching the UI-chrome-is-Indonesian convention while staying legible to English speakers.

nodes.label: Codebase Review (Efficiency, API Contract, Maintainability, Scalability)
nodes.rationale: Written as an executable work list for an implementing agent rather than prose: each finding states problem, why it matters, exact fix, and acceptance criteria, with a prescribed implementation order (quick wins → contract/compliance → efficiency → docs last, so docs describe the post-fix state).
nodes.norm_label: codebase review (efficiency, api contract, maintainability, scalability)

nodes.label: Standing Rules for the Implementer
nodes.rationale: Never weaken safety behavior (blocked path, force_append_disclaimer, bilingual coverage, prompt safety rules must stay at least as strict; when in doubt fail closed); preserve the services/routes/schemas layering; keep the app_state module-global patching pattern working; run pytest after each finding.

nodes.label: F1: Chat History Injected Twice into Every Prompt
nodes.rationale: MessagesPlaceholder('chat_history') and a {chat_history} slot in the human template both render the same message list, so every turn pays double token cost and the model additionally sees raw HumanMessage(content=...) repr text, degrading quality.
nodes.norm_label: f1: chat history injected twice into every prompt

nodes.label: F2: Blocking Sync Work on the Event Loop
nodes.rationale: Two paths: async upload_image calls classify_skin_image synchronously (PIL + TensorFlow predict freeze all concurrent SSE streams, and the lazy lru_cache model load makes the first upload absorb multi-second latency), and the Chroma retriever's blocking embed+query saturates LangChain's bounded sync thread pool. Fix is asyncio.to_thread for classification plus an end-to-end async retrieval path, keeping sync paths for the ingestion CLI.
nodes.norm_label: f2: blocking sync work on the event loop

nodes.label: F3: SessionMemory Grows Unbounded and Reads Without Its Lock
nodes.rationale: Turns are bounded per session but sessions are never evicted, and each upload mints a fresh UUID, so memory leaks linearly with unique sessions. add_turn locks but get_history does not — a latent race once eviction mutates the dict. Fix adds TTL + LRU eviction with time.monotonic and makes get_history async and lock-guarded.
nodes.norm_label: f3: sessionmemory grows unbounded and reads without its lock

nodes.label: F4: SSE Error Path Leaks Internals, Never Logs, Never Emits done
nodes.rationale: Four defects in one except block: str(e) is sent to the browser (information disclosure), nothing is logged server-side (undiagnosable failures), no terminal done frame (clients hang), and CancelledError on disconnect isn't an Exception so add_turn/log_query are silently skipped. The done frame must move to finally, but guarded so GeneratorExit on disconnect doesn't raise 'async generator ignored GeneratorExit'.
nodes.norm_label: f4: sse error path leaks internals, never logs, never emits done

nodes.label: F5: Client detection Field Is a Prompt-Injection Channel
nodes.rationale: Unconstrained client strings are model_dump_json'd into the SYSTEM prompt slot, so a crafted label can carry 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE' text into the highest-privilege position and undermine prompt rule 7. Fix constrains label to a Literal and model_version to a pattern, and renders detection explicitly instead of dumping JSON. The schema must duplicate the label values rather than import from services/ — layering rule — with a test asserting the two lists match.
nodes.norm_label: f5: client detection field is a prompt-injection channel

nodes.label: F6: Evidence Filter Fails Open When a Chunk Has No Score
nodes.rationale: metadata.get('score', 1.0) means a scoreless doc passes the gate. Latent today because the adapter always sets score, but a gate protecting medical answers should fail closed by construction, not by luck of the current backend. One-character fix: default 0.0.
nodes.norm_label: f6: evidence filter fails open when a chunk has no score

nodes.label: F7: Blocked Responses Skip Disclaimer, Logging, and Memory
nodes.rationale: Safety-blocked turns violate the stated 'disclaimer on every turn' guarantee, are invisible to compliance review because no log_query entry is written, and leave the model without context that it refused. Fix force-appends the disclaimer, logs with a new classification parameter passed from BOTH branches, and records the turn.
nodes.norm_label: f7: blocked responses skip disclaimer, logging, and memory

nodes.label: F8: SSE Chunk Schema Untyped; CitationOut Dead
nodes.rationale: The SSE event stream IS the public API contract of /api/chat, yet type is a bare str (typos ship silently) and citations are list[dict] despite a correctly-shaped CitationOut model sitting unused three lines below.
nodes.norm_label: f8: sse chunk schema untyped; citationout dead

nodes.label: F9: Citation Events Report Every Retrieved Chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitting on retriever completion means the UI shows sources the answer never used, extract_citations() is dead in the app path, and citations_used is hardcoded empty so the offline quality metric is permanently zero. Citations are only knowable after the token stream ends, so emission must move there.
nodes.norm_label: f9: citation events report every retrieved chunk

nodes.label: F10: Token Usage Logged as 0/0
nodes.rationale: ChatOpenAI(stream_usage=True) attaches usage_metadata to the final streamed chunk; that chunk has empty content so the existing `if token:` guard already skips emitting it. Without this, cost for an OpenAI-backed medical service is unmeasurable.

nodes.label: F11: Upload Buffers Unlimited Bytes and Leaks Paths
nodes.rationale: await file.read() buffers the entire body before the 10MB check, so a multi-GB upload is held in memory then rejected — a memory-exhaustion DoS. Also trusts client content_type, and the 503 detail interpolates FileNotFoundError which contains the server's model filesystem path.
nodes.norm_label: f11: upload buffers unlimited bytes and leaks paths

nodes.label: F12: session_id Is an Unvalidated Free-Form String
nodes.rationale: Sessions are minted server-side as UUID4 but /api/chat accepts any string, so histories can be read or poisoned by guessing and arbitrarily long ids become unbounded dict keys — which compounds F3. Format validation is explicitly a partial fix; true authorization is out of scope.
nodes.norm_label: f12: session_id is an unvalidated free-form string

nodes.label: F13: get_settings() Re-Parses .env on Every Call
nodes.rationale: Per-request filesystem read and parse, and worse, two call sites can observe different settings if .env changes mid-run. lru_cache is safe because tests construct Settings() directly or patch module globals.
nodes.norm_label: f13: get_settings() re-parses .env on every call

nodes.label: F14: SSE Translator Duck-Types the Retrieve Step
nodes.rationale: Matching 'the retrieve step' by checking whether the output dict contains retrieved_docs breaks silently if any future chain step carries that key, and the == [] sentinel cannot distinguish 'retriever returned nothing' from 'not seen yet'. Fix names the step via with_config(run_name='retrieve') and uses an explicit seen flag.
nodes.norm_label: f14: sse translator duck-types the retrieve step

nodes.label: F15: No Timeout Around the LLM Stream
nodes.rationale: A hung upstream call keeps the SSE connection, generator, and resources open indefinitely — slow-drip resource exhaustion during upstream incidents. Fixed with asyncio.timeout (Python 3.11) reusing F4's error-then-done path.
nodes.norm_label: f15: no timeout around the llm stream

nodes.label: F16: Missing SSE Anti-Buffering Headers; /health Lies Before Init
nodes.rationale: Without Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no, nginx buffers the stream and silently destroys the token-by-token UX. Separately, initialize_app_state happily builds a chain with an empty API key so a misconfigured deploy passes health checks and fails every request — hence a separate /ready readiness probe and a startup ValueError.
nodes.norm_label: f16: missing sse anti-buffering headers; /health lies before init

nodes.label: F17: Classifier Output Unguarded Against Shape and Logit Surprises
nodes.rationale: A different head width raises IndexError deep in the request and a logits head yields confidence > 1.0 which fails DetectionResult's le=1.0 as an opaque 500. Model swaps are expected here. Also flags for human verification that EfficientNetB3's canonical input is 300x300 while the code says 224 — explicitly do NOT change it without confirming against the trained artifact.
nodes.norm_label: f17: classifier output unguarded against shape and logit surprises

nodes.label: F18: Safety Keyword Checks Use Bare Substring Matching
nodes.rationale: 'film' matches 'biofilm' and 'stock' matches 'stockings', so legitimate skin queries get the canned off-topic refusal. False refusals on a medical education tool are a direct safety-quality regression, and this gate sits in front of every query. Word-boundary regexes still handle multi-word entries like 'tahi lalat' correctly.
nodes.norm_label: f18: safety keyword checks use bare substring matching

nodes.label: F19: PubMed Parsing Truncates Abstracts and Mangles Dates
nodes.rationale: t.text returns only text before the first child element, and PubMed abstracts routinely contain <i>/<sup>/<b>, so abstracts are silently truncated on the way into the knowledge base — degrading the exact corpus the RAG system exists to ground on. Also PubDate/Month is a name ('Jan') so zfill is a no-op, and joining 500 PMIDs into one efetch GET URL breaks precisely at the advertised max_results.
nodes.norm_label: f19: pubmed parsing truncates abstracts and mangles dates

nodes.label: F20: Log Rotation Not Multi-Worker Safe; All Paths CWD-Relative
nodes.rationale: The app only works when started from the repo root with a single worker: TimedRotatingFileHandler workers clobber each other's rotated files at midnight, and logs/templates/static/chroma/cache paths all resolve against CWD. Fix anchors everything to PROJECT_ROOT; for rotation, documenting the single-worker constraint is deemed acceptable rather than building a logging daemon.
nodes.norm_label: f20: log rotation not multi-worker safe; all paths cwd-relative

nodes.label: F21: CLAUDE.md, architecture.md, README Describe a Codebase That No Longer Exists
nodes.rationale: All three claim RAG lives in utils/, that there is no server-rendered UI, and that the classifier returns a hardcoded mock — all false. These docs steer humans AND coding agents, so drift is actively harmful; the review itself had to rediscover the real structure by reading source. Scheduled last so docs describe the post-fix state.
nodes.norm_label: f21: claude.md, architecture.md, readme describe a codebase that no longer exists

nodes.label: F22: O(n^2) Response Accumulation in the Token Loop
nodes.rationale: full_response += token copies the whole string per token; accumulate into a list and join once.
nodes.norm_label: f22: o(n^2) response accumulation in the token loop

nodes.label: F25: Dead Code (Unused Settings, Orphaned Accessor, Dead Template Context)
nodes.rationale: main.py's module-level settings forces a .env parse at import for no consumer; get_app_settings has zero callers; and chat_page builds session/label/confidence template context that chat.html never reads because the page pulls those from URL params in JS instead.
nodes.norm_label: f25: dead code (unused settings, orphaned accessor, dead template context)

nodes.label: F27: Magic Numbers Scattered Across Modules
nodes.rationale: max_turns=6, temperature=0.3, 1500-char truncation, and batch_size=100 are hardcoded at call sites while sibling knobs like rag_top_k live in Settings. Defaults preserved exactly so no existing test changes behavior.
nodes.norm_label: f27: magic numbers scattered across modules

nodes.label: F30: Pydantic v1 Relics on the Retriever Adapter
nodes.rationale: Inner `class Config` is deprecated under Pydantic v2 and emits warnings; underscore attrs rely on private-attr inference plus a custom __init__. Also the adapter is misplaced in app_state and belongs beside EvidenceFilteredRetriever in retriever.py.
nodes.norm_label: f30: pydantic v1 relics on the retriever adapter

nodes.label: F33: log_query Records Identical Retrieved/After-Filter Counts
nodes.rationale: The route only ever sees post-filter output, so the pre-filter count the log schema implies is unknowable there. Two options offered — stash the pre-filter count in doc metadata, or accept equality with an explicit comment — but the log schema keys must not change because downstream eval reads them.
nodes.norm_label: f33: log_query records identical retrieved/after-filter counts

nodes.label: Severity Rubric (High/Medium/Low)
nodes.rationale: High = wastes money/tokens per request, blocks the event loop, leaks data, breaks the client contract, or violates a stated compliance guarantee. Medium = degrades contract/observability/robustness under realistic conditions. Low = mechanical cleanup.

nodes.label: Eval Report
nodes.rationale: Template scaffold only — every metric cell still reads '_filled by run_eval.sh_', so no eval run has been recorded against it.

nodes.label: Eval Metrics Targets Table
nodes.rationale: Targets: recall@5 > 70%, disclaimer presence 100%, keyword coverage > 80%, ID/EN parity delta < 10%, p95 latency < 8s — the same numbers the RAG design spec set as success criteria.

nodes.label: Similarity Threshold Sweep
nodes.rationale: Sweeps 0.5/0.6/0.7/0.8 for recall@5. Recommendation rule is not 'maximize recall' but 'highest recall@5 that still produces quality citations' — recall alone would push the threshold to zero and defeat the evidence filter.

nodes.label: base.html Shared Layout
nodes.rationale: Defines blocks title / main_class / content / scripts, includes the navbar partial, and loads theme.js globally. Branded 'SkinVision' rather than the spec's generic naming.

nodes.label: Inline Theme Init Script (FOUC Guard)
nodes.rationale: A blocking IIFE in <head> reads localStorage then falls back to prefers-color-scheme and stamps `dark` on <html> before first paint, preventing a light-mode flash. It must run after the tailwind config declaration (which sets darkMode:'class') but before body renders.

nodes.label: chat.html Consultation Page
nodes.rationale: Overrides main_class to a fixed-height non-scrolling shell so only the chat area scrolls. Contains no Jinja expressions at all — session/label/confidence come from URL params read in chat.js, which is exactly the dead template context review F25 flags.

nodes.label: Chat SSE Mount Points (#chat-area, #chat-input, #send-btn)
nodes.rationale: Empty containers filled entirely by chat.js as SSE frames arrive; #prompt-bubbles is likewise populated client-side. The send button is disabled while streaming.

nodes.label: marked + DOMPurify Response Rendering
nodes.rationale: LLM output is rendered as markdown, so it must be sanitized before injection — DOMPurify is the XSS control for untrusted model text, matching the design spec's rule that output is always treated as text and never as executable instructions.

nodes.label: Chat Persistent Disclaimer Banner
nodes.rationale: Pinned above the input rather than in the scrollback so it can never scroll out of view — this is layer 3 of the three-layer disclaimer, the one that is independent of the LLM.

nodes.label: home.html Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Ships a centered hero, a 3-column icon feature grid, and a 'Powered by EfficientNetB3 + RAG' badge — all three explicitly on the design spec's AI-slop ban list, so the implementation diverged from §3.1. It does keep the spec's substantive content: the four lesion types and the 'Kapan Harus ke Dokter' criteria.

nodes.label: Four Lesion Type Cards
nodes.rationale: Karsinoma Sel Basal, Karsinoma Sel Skuamosa, Melanoma, Nevus — rendered in the corrected legacy label order, color-coded by severity (red/orange/red/green) to communicate risk without stating a diagnosis.

nodes.label: upload.html Intake Page
nodes.rationale: Drop zone with inline preview, photo-quality tips, and a detect button that stays disabled until a file is chosen. States (loading / error-card / result-card) are all pre-rendered hidden and toggled by upload.js.

nodes.label: Upload Error Card with Re-Upload Action
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the VLM validation gate's 400/503 rejections as a recoverable state with an explicit 'Unggah Ulang Gambar' path, rather than a dead-end alert — the detect button stays disabled after a validation error so the user must re-upload.
nodes.norm_label: upload error card with re-upload action

nodes.label: Classification Result Card
nodes.rationale: Shows label, confidence percentage, a confidence bar, a qualitative level, and the model version in monospace, with an inline amber 'Hasil AI Bisa Keliru' warning attached to the result itself. Auto-redirects to the chatbot rather than making the handoff a manual link.

nodes.label: disclaimer_bar.html Partial
nodes.rationale: Reusable amber left-bordered bar with an overridable `disclaimer_text` block. Appears unused by the shipped pages, which inline their own disclaimer-banner markup instead.

nodes.label: navbar.html Partial
nodes.rationale: Sticky backdrop-blur bar with Beranda/Deteksi links. Active state is computed server-side from `request.url.path`, which is why every UI route must pass `request` into the template context.

nodes.label: Navbar Theme Toggle Button
nodes.rationale: Calls a global toggleTheme() defined in theme.js and renders its icon into an empty #theme-icon span filled client-side, so the icon always matches the theme the inline head script already applied.
